# Global preferences — work kit (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)

## Commit style
- Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description`
- Imperative mood, subject ≤72 chars
- Types I use: feat, fix, refactor, docs, chore, test, style
- Commit autonomously when a discrete unit of work completes (a feature, a fix, a refactor) — don't wait for me to prompt


## Mid-session persistence (universal)
When we agree on something durable mid-conversation — a template, scoring rule, column spec, diagnostic framework, calibration, or prompt — write it to a file IMMEDIATELY, in the same turn. Don't batch to end of session.

The laptop can close abruptly (battery, distraction). Anything that needs to survive must already be on disk by then.

## At session start
Sweep ALL memory files under `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/memory/`, not just `MEMORY.md`'s index. The index lags behind file contents; individual files often hold durable decisions the index hasn't yet pointed to.

If unsure which slug corresponds to the current project, run `/memory` first to surface the loaded paths.

## Session wrap-up

When I signal end-of-session — by saying "wrap up", "save before I close", or any equivalent — run the following procedure in order, then stop. Chat transcripts don't persist between sessions; files, memory, and CLAUDE.md do.

### 1. Session log entry
Append a dated entry to the project's session log under a `## YYYY-MM-DD — open threads + decisions` heading. Cover:
- **Decided** — durable conclusions, not ephemeral thinking
- **In the air** — open threads that didn't resolve
- **Next session** — the first thing to pick up

Log file location:
- Otherwise create one at the project root named `SESSION_LOG.md`

### 2. Auto-memory updates
Open the project's memory dir at `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/memory/` and:
- Add new project-memory entries for in-flight work or shifts in plan
- Add new feedback-memory entries for durable preferences or calibrations from this session
- Update existing memory files that have drifted; remove stale ones
- Update `MEMORY.md` so its index reflects any new pointers
- **Budget compaction (keep loaded context bounded).** `MEMORY.md` and the project `CLAUDE.md` are auto-loaded every session and capped (~24 KB / 40 K chars; the `claude-md-size` hook warns on breach). When either nears its cap, offset growth — don't just append: for `MEMORY.md`, move Closed/Superseded/Historical lines into `MEMORY_ARCHIVE.md` (the topic file stays on disk, still recallable); for the project `CLAUDE.md`, condense the oldest settled rule to invariant + pointer, its detail migrating to a spec under `docs/`.

If unsure which slug corresponds to this project, run `/memory` first to confirm the loaded paths.

### 3. Persist sketched artifacts
Any durable artifact we sketched in chat — templates, scoring rules, column specs, diagnostic frameworks, prompts, schemas — write to an appropriate project file now. Nothing durable should be left only in chat.

### 4. Commit and push outstanding work
Run `git status`. Group the modified/untracked files by logical unit and commit each group with a Conventional Commit message.

Apply the secrets-scan guardrail from the Git autonomy section before pushing. If you deliberately leave anything uncommitted (half-finished experiment, scratch file), call it out explicitly in the summary below.

### 5. Confirm with a 3-line summary
Reply with exactly three lines:
- **Saved & pushed:** [commits made + files persisted this turn]
- **Pending:** [what's still in flight or deliberately uncommitted]
- **Next session:** [the first thing to pick up]

Then stop. Let me close the laptop.


## Coding behavior (agent discipline)
Complements — does not replace — the git/secrets rules above. Bias: reduce costly
mistakes on non-trivial work; on trivial edits, use judgment.

- **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the request requires. Don't "improve" adjacent
  code/comments/formatting; don't refactor what isn't broken; match existing style.
  Remove only orphans *your* change created; flag unrelated dead code, don't delete it.
- **Goal-driven execution.** Turn tasks into verifiable goals and loop until met
  ("fix the bug" -> "write a failing test, then make it pass"). Prefer conditions you
  prove by running something (test/lint/build exit code).
- **Simplicity first.** Minimum code that solves the problem; no speculative features,
  single-use abstractions, or unrequested config. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite.
- **State assumptions, don't stall.** On ambiguity, write the assumption and proceed;
  don't silently guess; block only when the choice is destructive or expensive to reverse.

> The secrets-scan guardrail above is now **enforced** by a PreToolUse hook
> (`~/.claude/hooks/secrets-scan.sh`), not just instruction.

## Agent fan-out memory guard (global · added 2026-07-05)


- **Pre-flight:** before launching a multi-agent workflow, check `free -h`; if available RAM < ~6 GB, shrink the fan-out or ask me to close heavy apps (Chrome) first.
- **Compact returns:** subagents return schema'd summaries; bulk content is written to files on disk with the agent returning paths — never raw page dumps into the parent.
- **Chunk heavy-content stages** into batches of 3–4 (heap is the constraint, not the CPU-derived concurrency cap).
- **RSS watcher on big runs:** background monitor that alerts when the claude process crosses ~7 GB → pause the workflow, persist state, resume later.
- **After any kill: resume, never re-run** — workflow journals persist to disk; `resumeFromRunId` replays the cached prefix free. Read the journal before assuming loss.
- **Machine layer:** laptop swap grown 2G→16G via `Orchestration/tools/grow-swap.sh` (re-runnable on any machine; verified live 7-05). Escalation if balloons recur: launch heavy sessions as `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh=10G claude` (throttles + swaps instead of getting killed).


## Operating doctrine — the 9 pillars (global, always-loaded)

Nine cross-project pillars (8 distilled from every repo in the ecosystem on 2026-06-26; the 9th is the
method that found them). This is the standing way I work — set here so none is ever re-derived.
A project **opts in** by declaring `brain-managed: true` near the top of its CLAUDE.md and
instantiating what it needs (scaffold: `Orchestration/templates/brain/`). Throwaway/`/tmp` work is exempt.

1. **Orchestration** — one version-controlled repo is the canonical `~/.claude`; `install.sh`
   *symlinks* what I own and jq-deep-merges only managed keys into the app-owned `settings.json`;
   the same rails deploy to laptop + VPS. (This repo.)
2. **Deterministic file-based brain** — knowledge lives in version-controlled markdown loaded
   *whole and identically* every session: a CLAUDE.md spine, immutable `raw/` evidence vs an editable
   `brain/` synthesis, append-only decisions + corrections-are-law ledgers, **auto-memory OFF** for
   brain-managed projects. **No vector/RAG over memory** (it reintroduces run-to-run non-determinism).
   *Repo-hygiene corollary (deliberately NOT its own pillar — covered by 2/5/9):*
   a repo root holds load-bearing + canonical files only; point-in-time artifacts (research, postmortems, old
   audits, scratch) live in `archive/` or `docs/`. **Never reorganize a working code layout for taste** (pillar
   5). Cleanup is a periodic pillar-9 audit, not continuous fuss.
3. **Layered, reachable knowledge** — operating truth in the spine; *capability* knowledge (how-to
   playbooks, deep research) distilled into auto-activating **Skills** + a greppable index — additive,
   never replaced. **Ritual: after any deep-research pass, distill it into a skill** so it is reachable
   later without being re-explained. Adopted skills/plugins are pinned in a manifest wired into `install.sh`.
4. **Remote / always-on ops** — two non-mixing auth planes (keyless authorship + a keyed always-on
   VPS); harden-before-keys; systemd timers / GitHub-Actions cron; cost-routed via ccr with an external
   ground-truth identity verifier (`ccr-which` — see *model identity* above); ff-only sync; outputs
   pushed to git for mobile.
5. **Spec-driven, test-pinned engineering ("rule + code move together")** — durable behavior is a dated
   spec (with rejected alternatives) → test-first execution → **locked by a pure lib + a unit test + a CI
   gate, the doc rule changing in the SAME commit as the code**. *The render IS the display* (paste
   verbatim, never recall). Extends *Coding behavior* above with this lock-in-code clause.
6. **Autonomous build factory** — run a repo as a self-feeding loop: private spec = authority, a
   public-safe map carries context, work = labeled GitHub issues an agent picks; **the CI/review
   pipeline IS the reviewer** → auto-merge → deploy → smoke → self-schedule; humans see only flagged items.
7. **Grounded, cost-bounded LLM engineering** — minimal LLM surface (shrink the model's mandate, render
   the rest deterministically + guardrail + test); cite-or-refuse (render "—/no signal", never fabricate);
   deterministic-prune + confirm-before-spend + cheap→expensive cascade + decide-once ledgers; sponsored
   compute behind ONE server-side chokepoint (fail-closed monthly cap / fail-open per-user cap / model
   allowlist). Read model facts from the `claude-api` skill, not memory.
8. **Adversarial security & exposure-safety** — assume every reader is hostile: enforcement in the data
   layer (RLS + edge functions; client checks are decoration); secrets only in deploy env / register-by-
   location; anonymize at the build boundary; public/private path-guard + a re-runnable exposure audit;
   read-only credential-free investigation. Extends the git/secrets guardrail above.
9. **Subagentic audit-and-remediate ("investigate before you change")** — to improve a system, don't patch
   blind. Run a **subagentic deep audit** (fan out read-only agents per area/repo) + inventory the internal
   tools + research external best-practice, then **adversarially VERIFY every finding** (kill the plausible-
   but-wrong — this is what catches even my own errors), synthesize a **prioritized, risk-rated** plan
   (separate *safe-now* from *touches-fragile*), and apply fixes **one at a time, each independently verified**
   (test / golden-diff / live-run), rule + code moving together. **Right-size the fan-out to the task** —
   full rigor where the risk is, lean where it isn't. This is the meta-pillar that produces the other eight;
   exemplar: the 2026-06-26 ecosystem audit (5 repos, 57→43 findings, 14 killed by the verify pass).

## Writing doctrine — anti-slop / STE (global, added 2026-08-17)

All prose deliverables — docs, reports, READMEs, PR text, presentations, summaries, session logs —
follow the `ste-writing` skill (source: ASD-STE100 Issue 9 + the woosal1337 anti-slop kit; evidence:
STE cut slop violations 74% on Claude, beat Orwell's rules and banned-word lists). Defaults:

- **English is the default working language**; Spanish deliverables (client work) use the skill's
  Spanish-adaptation section. **STE-flavored** mode for general prose; **strict** mode for
  procedures, runbooks, and error messages.
- Always-on core: one idea per sentence (max 20 words instruction / 25 descriptive), active voice,
  simple tenses, one term per concept (never rotate synonyms), short common words, no marketing
  adjectives, no filler openers, no semicolons.
- **Lint English drafts** with `~/.claude/skills/ste-writing/ste-lint.py` before delivery when the
  text matters (flavored < 2.5 violations/100w, strict < 1.5). Spanish: manual checklist in the skill.
- Domain terms are legal: STE's "technical nouns/verbs" mechanism approves project-glossary
  vocabulary (topper, stockist, wholesale…) — police the sentence rules, not the domain words.
- Form is half the cure. Pair it with the substance check (pillar 7 cite-or-refuse; label every
  figure dato/estimación) — STE fixes how it reads, the labels fix whether it is true. A clean
  sentence about an unverified number is still bullshit. Per the STEMG AI White Paper: AI supports,
  never overrides, the standard; accountability stays with the human author.

**Precedence (conflict rule):** when a rule appears in more than one place, the **auto-loaded CLAUDE.md
copy wins** — it is the one most likely to be in context; memory files and specs carry the longer-form
rationale, not a competing source of truth.

## Work profile (generated kit — this section exists only on work machines)

### Boundary (two directions)
This kit is generic method: doctrine, hooks, skills, ledgers. It carries nothing about any employer, and nothing employer-specific may ever be added to it or to the private repo that generates it. In the other direction, nothing personal lives in the employer workspace: the employer's context, notes and mirrors live in the employer project, never here. Lessons learned at work that improve the method go to `FOLLOWUPS.md` in the kit clone and travel back by hand.

### Git at work
- Never clone, push, fetch or run anything against the company version control. The user does that.
- Never edit read-only code copies. They are evidence, not a workspace.
- In the notes repo: commit when a discrete unit of work completes, without asking. Push only when asked. Anything destructive (reset, rebase, force, delete): ask first.
- Never override the repo's git identity. The author comes from the repo or machine config, never from this kit.
- The secrets-scan hook gates every `git commit` and `git push` and fails closed. A real hit is fixed at the source: scrub the generator with `tools/redact-secrets.py`, move the value to an env var, or delete it. Never allowlist a whole directory. `.secrets-scan-allow` is for individual fixtures and examples only.

### Memory layers
Three layers may coexist: auto-memory, a handoff plugin, and session logs. The rule that keeps them from drifting: a durable fact goes to the notes repo, in git, in the same turn it is learned. Auto-memory holds preferences only. The handoff plugin holds in-flight state only. When two layers disagree, the git-tracked note wins.

### Wrap-up at work
If the project has its own wrap skill, run it. The wrap-up list above (session log, memory updates, persist sketched artifacts, commit) is the checklist of what must be on disk before the session ends. Pushing is not part of it here.

### Local profile
Machine-specific profile ("who I am here", tools, house rules) lives in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.local.md`. It is imported below and is never part of the kit. `install.sh` created it from any pre-existing global CLAUDE.md.
